subtitles.text: Passage 2 My Very Cool Computer Reading Exercise After you have read passage 2, listen to me read.
Read along with me as you listen.
My computer is very cool.
I use it to study, play games, watch movies, and do my 3D.
Modeling and graphic design work.
The computer is inside a tall tower case with clear glass on the side.
I can see the parts inside.
There are colorful RGB lights.
Lights inside, and they slowly change color.
The tower sits on my desk next to my monitor.
Inside the tower, the most important part is the motherboard.
All other parts connect to it.
I have the latest motherboard and it supports the newest PCIe 5.0 and DDR5 technology.
It has many slots and ports for hardware.
It also has a fast chipset that helps all the parts talk to each other.
In the middle of the motherboard is the CPU.
The CPU is the brain of the computer.
My computer uses a very powerful CPU with many cores and threads.
These cores allow the computer to do many tasks at the same time.
When I edit graphical elements for work or play a game for fun, the CPU works very fast.
It sits in a socket on the motherboard, and over it there is a large liquid cooling system.
This cooler keeps the CPU temperature low when the computer works hard.
Next to the CPU, there are four sticks of RAM.
The RAM is the working memory of the computer.
My computer has 32 gigabytes of DDR5 RAM with a very high clock speed.
Programs move data in and out of the RAM very quickly.
This helps games load faster and helps large programs run smoothly.
Another important part is the GPU.
It is connected to the PCIe slot on the motherboard.
I have a large, powerful GPU to do my design work and play graphics-intensive AAA games.
The GPU is also used for internet browsing, HDR movies, 3D rendering, and AI acceleration.
It has many CUDA cores, a lot of VRAM, and advanced ray tracing hardware.
When I play the latest games, I can turn the graphics options to maximum.
For storage, my computer uses several NVMe SSD drives.
These drives connect through the M2 interface on the motherboard.
The SSD has very fast read speed and write speed.
Because of this, the operating system starts in just a few seconds.
Load times on programs and games are very short.
Most programs start instantly.
At the bottom of the tower is the power supply unit, or PSU.
The PSU gives electricity to all the components.
It is a high wattage modular PSU.
So the cables are neat and organized.
Good power management keeps the system stable.
The tower also has many case fans for airflow.
The fans pull cool air into the case and push out hot air.
Together with the liquid cooling radiator, the whole system stays cool even when I am running intensive games.
Or programs.
I have some great peripherals too.
My main display is a large OLED 4K monitor with a high refresh rate.
The colors are bright.
and the black color is very deep.
When the GPU sends frames to the monitor, the picture looks smooth and clear at 120 frames per second, or FPS.
In front of the monitor is my mechanical keyboard.
On a mechanical keyboard, each key has a mechanical switch.
The keys are big and make a sound when you press them.
It is easy to type quickly.
The keyboard also has programmable macros, which help when I code or play games.
Near the monitor, I have two stereo speakers, a high-precision gaming mouse, and a USB hub.
Sometimes I use a high quality microphone and webcam for online meetings.
All these devices connect through fast USB-C ports on the computer.
I built this desktop myself and I love using it.
When new components come out, I will upgrade it.
How about you?
What internal and external components does your computer have?
Did you understand the passage?
Did you understand all of the acronyms?
Please listen and read again.
Be sure to look at the key vocabulary when you do not understand.
When you are ready, take the reading comprehension quiz.
Gambate.
